I. Background and Discussion 
The Federal Trade Commission ("FTC" or "Commission") is taking final action in light of 
Federal court decisions vacating the Commission's final rules in three of the Commission's 
recent rulemaking proceedings. These decisions vacated final rules revising the Negative 
Option Rule and promulgating the CARS Rule and the Non-Compete Rule. Each will be 
discussed in turn. 
A. The Negative Option Rule-16 CFR Part 425 
(https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-16/part-425) 
The Commission first promulgated the Negative Option Rule in 1973 pursuant to the FTC 
Act, 15 U.S.C. 41 (https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/15/41) et seq., finding that some 
negative option marketers were engaged in unfair and deceptive practices that violated 
section 5 of the Act, 15 U.S.C. 45 (https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/15/45)_l7l On 
November 15, 2024, the Commission published a final rule ("2024 Rule") amending its 
Negative Option Rule.I2I Among other things, the 2024 Rule (1) prohibited 
misrepresentations of any material fact made while marketing using negative option 
features; (2) required sellers to provide important information prior to obtaining 
consumers' billing information and charging consumers; (3) required sellers to obtain 
consumers' unambiguously affirmative consent to the negative option feature prior to 
charging them; and (4) required sellers to provide consumers with simple cancellation 
mechanisms to immediately halt all recurring charges. 
After the 2024 Rule was published, businesses and industry groups asked four Federal 
circuit courts to review the Negative Option Rule. The Judicial Panel on Multidistrict 
Litigation consolidated their petitions in the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Eighth Circuit.I3I 
Petitioners argued that the 2024 Rule did not meet the specificity and prevalence 
requirements of section 18 of the FTC Act,I4I violated section 22 of the FTC Act 151 because 
the Commission had not issued a preliminary regulatory analysis, and was overbroad and 
unworkable.I6I The Eighth Circuit found that the Commission's failure to issue a preliminary 
regulatory analysis was "procedurally insufficient" and vacated the 2024 Rule.I7I 
In light of the Eighth Circuit's vacatur, this final rule revises the Negative Option Rule to 
restore it in the form it existed before the 2024 Rule became effective.I8I See Menorah Med.
